1.why: All eight screens show a static, uncluttered layout with no moving images, animations, or pop-ups.

2.why: Bold headings and solid blue primary buttons stand out clearly against the white cards and light background.

3.why: The linear single-purpose screens make the next required action obvious, though the persistent Logs panel adds minor visual noise.

4.why: The user must recall a multi-step recovery sequence and the full password-complexity rule set with no memory aids.

5.why: No password-manager, autofill, or “remember me” controls appear on any screen.

6.why: Apart from one pre-filled email address, the interface shows no saved or familiar items the user could recognize.

7.why: Instructional text is concise, uses plain language, and is easy to read on every step.

8.why: No error messages are present in any of the provided screenshots, so the claim cannot be verified as true.

9.why: Password rules are stated but no example values are shown; other fields likewise lack illustrative examples.

10.why: The flow never offers or explains alternative authentication choices such as face login versus password or code.

11.why: Each screen presents only one primary action and at most one secondary button, avoiding choice overload.

12.why: Green confirmation banners and explicit success pages (e.g., “Appointment request received”) clearly state the result of each action.

13.why: A few safety tips and requirement notes exist, yet most new steps lack contextual help or short guidance tips.

14.why: A visible “Start over” button on the code-entry screen lets the user restart after a mistake.

15.why: Identical header, card layout, button styling, and logs panel are maintained across all eight steps.
